chunks: Al-Tawhid: My father, from Sa'd, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ruba'i ibn Abdallah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described (as He really is). He said: Zurara said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be described with incapacity. How can He be described when He has said in His Book: 'And they have not estimated Allah with true estimation'? Thus, He is not described with power except that He is greater than that.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah cannot be described?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tawhid elucidates the Shia doctrine of divine incomparability (tanzih), asserting that Allah's essence transcends all human attributes. Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Baqir argue that since humans fail to estimate Allah's true power, any attribute ascribed to Him is inherently limited and thus surpassed by His infinite reality. This reinforces the theological principle that divine attributes are not comparable to created qualities.
